1.Nf3 d5 2.g3 c6 3.Bg2 Nf6 4.O-O Bf5 5.d.strategy: Develops the last minor piece to the square that supports e4 and keeps the c-pawn free to move. White now has everything ready to challenge Black's centre with either pawn, and keeps the position flexible.
1.Nf3 d5 2.g3 c6 3.Bg2 Nf6 4.O-O Bf5 5.d.name: King's Indian Attack, with Bf5

1.Nf3 d5 2.g3 c6 3.Bg2 Nf6 4.O-O Bf5 5.d.strategy: Hits the bishop at once: Black must retreat it or trade it for the knight, which hands White the bishop pair. But the knight stands on the rim with few good squares, and the central development waits; an ambitious idea the simple development does not need.
1.Nf3 d5 2.g3 c6 3.Bg2 Nf6 4.O-O Bf5 5.d.name: King's Indian Attack, with Bf5
